args.text:
Analysis of Intersection Size:
Let $C_A$ and $C_B$ be the connectivity sets for Ali and Baba, respectively. Since each merchant sells $k$ items and has a distinct selling stall ($S_i$) and buying stall ($B_i$) for each item, the size of each connectivity set is $|C_A| = |C_B| = 2k$ (assuming minimal internal overlap, which is the most generous assumption for maximizing set size).
We are looking for the smallest $k$ such that $|C_A \cap C_B| \ge 2$ is guaranteed, regardless of stall placement, given $N=7396$.

By the Pigeonhole Principle, the maximum possible size of the union is $|C_A \cup C_B| = |C_A| + |C_B| - |C_A \cap C_B| = 4k - |C_A \cap C_B|$.
To guarantee an intersection of at least 2 (i.e., $|C_A \cap C_B| \ge 2$), we must ensure that the worst-case scenario (where $|C_A \cap C_B| = 1$) exceeds the total number of available stalls $N$.
If $|C_A \cap C_B| = 1$, then $|C_A \cup C_B| = 4k - 1$.
We require $4k - 1 > N$.
$4k > N + 1$
$k > (7396 + 1) / 4$
$k > 7397 / 4$
$k > 1849.25$.
The smallest integer $k$ satisfying this condition is $k=1850$.
